field.label: Enable MCP Endpoint
field.comment: Serves the Model Context Protocol endpoint at /magenx-mcp/server. While disabled the endpoint returns 404 and advertises nothing. Requires a Magento Integration whose ACL role includes "AI MCP Server".

field.label: Allow Write Tools
field.comment: When No, tools that change data are not listed and cannot be called; the endpoint is read-only. This is independent of the integration's ACL — both must permit the write.

field.label: Allowed IP Addresses
field.comment:
Comma or newline separated. Plain addresses (203.0.113.7) and CIDR ranges (10.0.0.0/8) are supported. Leave empty to accept any source address that presents a valid token.
Behind a reverse proxy this compares against REMOTE_ADDR, which is the proxy's own address unless nginx's real_ip module is rewriting it (set_real_ip_from / real_ip_header). Without that, filling this in locks the endpoint out entirely. Refusals are recorded with the observed address in var/log/magenx_ai_mcp.log.

field.label: Allowed Browser Origins
field.comment: Comma or newline separated, e.g. https://app.example.com. The MCP transport requires the Origin header to be validated against DNS-rebinding attacks. Requests that send no Origin — curl, Claude Code, every ordinary MCP client — are unaffected by this setting. Requests that send one are refused unless it is listed here, so empty means "no browser may call this endpoint".

field.label: Writable Configuration Paths
field.comment: Comma or newline separated glob patterns, e.g. magenx_*/* or catalog/frontend/*. Empty denies every configuration write. Secret-bearing paths (keys, passwords, tokens, encrypted values) are refused regardless of what is listed here.

field.label: Tool Calls per Minute
field.comment: Per caller: one integration, or one admin across all their OAuth connections. A call over the limit is answered with an error the agent can read and wait on, and the first refusal in each minute is logged. 0 disables the limit.

field.label: Write Calls per Minute
field.comment: Confirmed write-tool calls per caller, counted on top of the limit above. Previews (a write called without confirm) count only towards the limit above. 0 disables the limit.

field.label: Audit Reads
field.comment: Writes are always recorded in var/log/magenx_ai_mcp.log. This adds successful reads to the same file: the tool, the integration, the arguments and the ids of the records returned — never the records themselves. "Personal data only" covers customers, orders and their documents, carts, returns, help desk tickets, GDPR requests and admin users.

group.label: OAuth
group.comment: Lets claude.ai, Claude Desktop and other MCP clients connect with an admin's own sign-in instead of an integration token. The admin approves each connection on a consent page behind the normal admin login and two-factor check, and the client acts with that admin's role. Clients are created, connections listed and revoked, and the optional connector key generated under System > Extensions > AI MCP Connections. See the README for the nginx locations this needs.

field.label: Enable OAuth
field.comment: Publishes /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, and accepts OAuth access tokens on the MCP endpoint. Integration tokens keep working either way.

field.label: Allow Dynamic Client Registration
field.comment: Leave this off. Create a client under System > Extensions > AI MCP Connections instead, and enter its client ID and secret in the connector's advanced settings ("Use your own OAuth client"). When on, anyone can register a client and start a flow: that reveals the admin URL to them, and lets them send an admin a consent link that would connect their Claude account to the admin's role.

field.label: Allowed Redirect URIs
field.comment: One per line, matched exactly. A client can only be created or registered with, and only ever receive an authorization code at, a URI listed here. The default is claude.ai's callback. Add other clients' callbacks only for services you trust with an admin's access.

field.label: Allow Loopback Redirects
field.comment: Accept http://localhost, http://127.0.0.1 and http://[::1] callbacks on any port, for clients that run on the admin's own machine (Claude Code, MCP Inspector). Any program on that machine can then complete a flow the admin approves.

field.label: Access Token Lifetime (minutes)
field.comment: 5 to 1440. The client renews it with its refresh token without asking the admin.

field.label: Connection Lifetime (days)
field.comment: 1 to 90, counted from approval and never extended by use. When it runs out the admin has to sign in, and pass two-factor authentication, again.

field.label: Public Base URL
field.comment: The origin clients reach the MCP endpoint on, e.g. https://www.example.com, when that is not the default store's secure base URL. It becomes part of the issuer and of every token's audience, so changing it ends every existing connection.

group.label: Tools
group.comment: These narrow what a client is shown, not what it is permitted to do. The integration's ACL role and the write switch still decide that, and a tool withheld here is withheld from every integration.

field.label: Enabled Tool Domains
field.comment: Select nothing to offer every domain, which is the default. Selecting some offers only those: the whole tool list is a large part of a client's context window, and an agent given only the domains its task needs plans better within it. A tool outside the selection is not listed and cannot be called.

field.label: Disabled Tools
field.comment: Comma or newline separated tool names, e.g. delete_product, delete_category. Applied after the domain selection above, so a name listed here is withheld even if its domain is enabled. A name no tool answers to is refused when you save rather than accepted and ignored.
